title: case-source officiality audit
spec_ref: specs/CALC-KIMI-K3-GPT56-JUDGE-001.spec.md (aggregators permitted for discovery/citation metadata only; a case record whose excerpt grounds a substantive proposition must be anchored to an official source)
method: Every CIT-REAL-* record in sources.jsonl hosted on a non-official domain was checked for the same opinion on an official California judicial-branch source (primarily https://www4.courts.ca.gov/opinions/archive/<docket>.PDF, the pattern already used by CIT-REAL-18/19/18-B/19-B; also courts.ca.gov/opinion/published/<date>/<docket>, courts.ca.gov site search, and the Wayback Machine for once-live official pages). Where an official source was found, the record's existing excerpt was compared against the fetched official text after whitespace normalization only (no other normalization, e.g. quote-mark style or letter case, was applied) to decide a verbatim match. Three sonnet subagents performed the fetching/comparison in parallel (per this repo's model-routing convention: source fetching/extraction on sonnet); this report reflects Fable-level synthesis and the final decision on each record. CIT-REAL-11 does not exist in the registry (never allocated) and is not an omission.

cit_index_determination.determination: SKIPPED_PER_INSTRUCTIONS — allowed aggregator use, not audited for re-anchoring
cit_index_determination.reasoning: All 9 CIT-INDEX-* records are courtlistener.com official-reporter volume/citation-index pages, and each record's own publication_or_precedential_status field already states verbatim: 'Official-reporter citation index metadata (CourtListener); used for citation-metadata verification only, not as the source of a substantive legal proposition.' They exist to supply negative evidence (confirming that a fabricated or miscited case citation does not correspond to a real holding in that reporter volume/page window), not to ground an affirmative substantive proposition. This is exactly the discovery/citation-metadata aggregator use the spec permits (specs/CALC-KIMI-K3-GPT56-JUDGE-001.spec.md: 'CourtListener or other aggregators may assist discovery and citation metadata but cannot alone establish a proposition, effective date, or precedential status'). No re-anchoring action was taken or required for these 9 records.

records.notes: Docket resolved to S095000 (cross-checked scocal.stanford.edu, CourtListener, Casemine — consistent). Tried https://www4.courts.ca.gov/opinions/archive/S095000.PDF and path variants (.pdf, /documents/, /cms/opinions/archive/, /opinions/archive/2002/) — all 404. supreme.courts.ca.gov case page — 404. appellatecases.courtinfo.ca.gov docket search — blocked by Cloudflare bot challenge (403) to both curl and WebFetch. Boundary-tested the live archive's real coverage window using known dockets: pre-2015 dockets (S171845 2011, S147345 2009, S140741 2011) all 404; 2017+ dockets (S227228, S235968) return 200. This 2002 opinion falls before that window. courts.ca.gov's own opinions page points historical researchers to a subscription LexisNexis database (not a .ca.gov domain), which does not qualify as official web hosting. Record left untouched (aggregator-hosted, caveat for reviewers).

Docket S133805. Tried https://www4.courts.ca.gov/opinions/archive/S133805.PDF (and www./courts.ca.gov/lowercase variants) — 404. Wayback Machine CDX/availability query for that exact path — zero snapshots ever recorded (page never crawled, unlike the Sargon case below). Legacy 'archopinions.htm' pre-2015 archive page — retired/404. appellatecases.courtinfo.ca.gov — 403 (bot-blocked). WebSearch site:courts.ca.gov for S133805/Taus — no opinion-PDF hits. 2007 opinion, pre-archive-coverage era. Record left untouched.

Official source exists and is live, but the stored excerpt does not appear verbatim (whitespace-normalized only) in it. Two discrepancies found: (1) caption case — stored excerpt reads 'Gregory GEISER, Plaintiff and Appellant, v. Peter KUHNS et al., Defendants and Appellants.' (mixed case, aggregator convention); the official opinion's caption is fully capitalized: 'GREGORY GEISER, Plaintiff and Appellant, v. PETER KUHNS et al., Defendants and Appellants.' (2) quotation-mark style — stored excerpt uses single quotes ('a disturbing increase' / 'lawsuits brought primarily...'); the official opinion uses double quotes throughout ("a disturbing increase" ... "lawsuits brought primarily to chill the valid exercise of the constitutional rights of freedom of speech and petition for the redress of grievances."). Word content is identical in both places; only case and quote-glyph differ, but the task's verbatim rule authorizes whitespace normalization only, not case-folding or quote-style normalization, so this is a genuine (if cosmetic) mismatch. Record NOT modified per instructions — flagged for reviewers, who may choose to correct the stored excerpt's typography to match the official opinion and then re-anchor in a follow-up pass, since the underlying legal content is confirmed accurate and the official PDF is live and reachable.

APPLIED to sources.jsonl. Official PDF confirmed live (HTTP 200, 36 pp., docket S227228). Excerpt 'This is a representative action seeking civil penalties on behalf of the State of California and aggrieved employees statewide for alleged wage and hour violations.' verified as an exact verbatim substring (whitespace-normalized) of the official opinion text. canonical_url, retrieved_at, and discovery_notes were updated; source_id, locator, excerpt, and sha256 were left byte-identical. This is the only CIT-REAL record in the audit that both had a discoverable official source AND passed the strict verbatim check.

records.case: Wilson v. Cable News Network, Inc.
records.notes: Official source exists and is live. The single quoted factual sentence in the stored excerpt — 'Plaintiff Stanley Wilson began working for Cable News Network, Inc., in 1996, and wrote and produced stories for the network for more than 17 years.' — IS verbatim in the official opinion (Part I). However, the rest of the stored excerpt is not: the caption block and reporter-citation string are vLex citation-service metadata, not court text (the official caption differs in case/formatting), and the excerpt's 'Held:' sentence is a paraphrase, not verbatim opinion language — the official opinion's actual holding reads 'We hold otherwise. The statute contains no exception for discrimination or retaliation claims, and ... the plaintiff's allegations about the defendant's invidious motives will not shield the claim from the same preliminary screening for minimal merit that would apply to any other claim arising from protected activity,' whereas the stored excerpt's 'Held:' clause inserts the word 'categorical' and restructures the sentence. Because the excerpt field as a whole does not pass verbatim, this is EXCERPT_MISMATCH, not re_anchored. Record NOT modified — flagged for reviewers, who could re-anchor to the confirmed-live official PDF above once the excerpt is trimmed to only the verbatim-verified sentence or corrected to quote the opinion's actual holding language.

records.case: Sargon Enterprises, Inc. v. University of Southern California
records.notes: SPECIAL CASE — flagging for reviewer attention. Docket S191550, decided 2012-11-26. https://www4.courts.ca.gov/opinions/archive/S191550.PDF returns 404 TODAY, confirming the pre-existing discovery_notes on this record. However, the Wayback Machine's availability API shows this exact official path was live and crawled: http://www.courts.ca.gov/opinions/archive/S191550.PDF, captured 2014-04-15, HTTP 200. That Wayback capture was fetched directly and confirmed to be the genuine 44-page slip opinion (docket S191550, filed 11/26/12); the stored excerpt's quoted proposition ('A small dental implant company that had net profits of $101,000 in 1998 has sued a university for breach of a contract...') is an exact verbatim match (whitespace-normalized) against that archived official text. Disposition kept as NO_OFFICIAL_HOSTING rather than re_anchored because there is currently no live, directly-resolving .ca.gov URL to set as canonical_url — pointing canonical_url at a web.archive.org mirror would substitute one non-.ca.gov domain for another, even though the underlying content is verified-authentic official text. Recommend to reviewers as a strong candidate for a follow-up 'historical-official, archived-only' re-anchoring policy decision (not made unilaterally here).

residual_open_items_for_b8: 13 CIT-REAL-* records remain aggregator-hosted with NO_OFFICIAL_HOSTING confirmed after real attempts (mostly pre-2015 California Supreme Court opinions and pre-1993 Court of Appeal opinions that predate the electronic archive) — these should carry an explicit aggregator caveat in the B8 reviewer bundles rather than be treated as fully primary-source-anchored.

2 records (CIT-REAL-3, CIT-REAL-15) have a live official source available but their stored excerpt fails strict verbatim comparison on typography/paraphrase grounds — B8 or a follow-up pass should decide whether to correct the excerpt text (case/quote-style for CIT-REAL-3; trim-to-verbatim-sentence or requote for CIT-REAL-15) and then re-anchor, since the underlying legal content in both cases was independently confirmed accurate.

1 record (CIT-REAL-16) has verified-authentic official content only via a Wayback Machine capture of a now-dead courts.ca.gov URL; needs a reviewer/architecture decision on whether an archived capture of an official source may serve as a canonical_url before this can move past NO_OFFICIAL_HOSTING.
